definition: Automatic Speech Recognition: converting audio into text.
details: Automatic Speech Recognition: converting audio into text. Modern ASR is end-to-end neural (audio in, tokens out), with the main architectural split being offline encoder-decoder models vs. streaming transducers.

explainer.lead: STT, or automatic speech recognition, converts audio into text. Modern ASR is end-to-end neural, taking audio in and emitting tokens out, with the main architectural split between offline encoder-decoder models and streaming transducers.

tiers.eli5: It's a program that listens to a recording or a live voice and types out the words it hears.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose between offline encoder-decoder models and streaming transducers depending on whether audio arrives in full or continuously. The split matters because streaming requires emitting tokens as audio arrives.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as automatic speech recognition converting audio into text; modern ASR is end-to-end neural, with the main architectural split between offline encoder-decoder models and streaming transducers. No formula or accuracy limits are stated.

explainer.example: An audio clip is fed into an end-to-end neural ASR system, which outputs the sequence of text tokens it heard.
